title: Lamb Saagwala
subtitle: Slow-cooked lamb shoulder with spinach and garam masala
excerpt: Diced lamb shoulder simmered until tender in a spiced sauce, then finished with wilted spinach. A rich, filling curry that rewards patience.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian restaurant tradition. Saagwala refers to a meat curry finished with spinach, common across northern India and Pakistan.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the spinach. Add fresh spinach when reheating for a better colour and texture.
recipe.batchNotes: The lamb base doubles well. Freeze the extra base and add spinach on the day of serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the lamb base a day ahead. Reheat on the hob and stir in the spinach just before serving.

content.text: Lamb saagwala is a slow-cooked lamb curry finished with spinach at the end. It gives deep, rounded flavour from the long braise. The spinach should go in right at the end to keep its colour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over a high heat. Brown the lamb in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per batch. Set aside.
Reduce to a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until deeply golden. Stir often.
Stir in the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return the lamb to the pot. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, and salt. Stir well and bring to a simmer.
Cover with a lid and cook over a low heat for 1 hour, until the lamb is tender and falling apart. Stir every 20 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce slightly.
Stir in the spinach in handfuls. Cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Stir in the garam masala, taste, and adjust salt. Top with coriander if using.

items.symptom: The lamb is still tough after 1 hour.
items.cause: Shoulder needs longer or the simmer was too gentle.
items.fix: Continue cooking, covered, for another 20 to 30 minutes on a steady low simmer. Add a splash of water if the sauce is too thick.

items.symptom: The spinach turns dull and brown.
items.cause: It was added too early or cooked too long.
items.fix: Add the spinach right at the end and stir just until wilted. Take the pan off the heat as soon as it collapses.

items.symptom: The sauce is very thin after removing the lid.
items.cause: The lamb released a lot of liquid during the braise.
items.fix: Cook uncovered over a medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.
